result.gateLogic:
THE CANONICAL PURE FUNCTION — reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result: ReviewResult): string[] at src/cli.ts:5150-5163. Builds reasons[] purely from result.qualityGate: (1) if gate.status==="failed" pushes `qualityGate.status=failed`; (2) for each non-empty gate.blockingConcerns[] pushes the trimmed concern verbatim; (3) for each gate.dimensions[] where dimension.status==="failed" OR dimension.risk==="high" pushes `${dimension.dimension} ${status}/${risk}: ${finding}`. Returns [] when nothing blocks. NOTE: it ONLY ever reads qualityGate — never frAcFindings, never sourceMutationDetected, never escalations. THIS is RE-2's downgrade point.

THREE CALL SITES (all must keep byte-identical no-skeptic behavior):
1) readLatestReviewGate(store, slice, verifier) at src/cli.ts:4915-4985 — THE ACCEPT GATE. Returns {passed, reason, status?, evidenceId?}. Reads latest review_result evidence (store.listEvidence(slice.id).filter(kind==="review_result" && payload.reviewResult).at(-1)). Order of checks (each returns early): no evidence -> passed:true "no review result recorded"; schema parse fail -> blocked; [BACKSTOP] parsed.sourceMutationDetected OR payload.sourceMutationsAfter[].mutated -> passed:false status:"human_required" "latest review detected immutable source mutation" (4937-4944); status!=="accepted" -> blocked with that status; [BACKSTOP] nonPassingRefs = slice.frAcRefs where reviewFindingForRef(frAcFindings,ref)?.status !== "passed" -> blocked "non-passing FR/AC findings" (4953-4961); stubOrHardcodeRisk==="high" -> blocked (4962); FINALLY qualityBlockingReasons = reviewQualityBlockingReasons(parsed.data) at 4970 -> if length>0 blocked "latest review quality gate failed: <joined ;>" (4970-4978); else passed:true "latest review accepted". RE-2 changes ONLY the 4970 step (consult skeptic before deciding length>0) — every backstop above (4937 mutation, 4953 frAc, plus schema-missing) stays untouched. readLatestReviewGate already takes (store, slice, verifier) so it can pass them to a slice/store-aware wrapper without signature change.
2) applyReviewOutcome(input:{store,slice,actor,result,reviewEvidenceId,sourceMutationsAfter}) at src/cli.ts:4682-4774. qualityBlockingReasons = reviewQualityBlockingReasons(input.result) at 4691; effectiveStatus = sourceMutationDetected?"human_required" : (status repair_required|human_required? keep : qualityBlockingReasons.length>0?"blocked":status). At 4703-4712 inserts a "blocker" escalation "Sleuth Review Gate blocked acceptance." with reasons joined. This runs at REVIEW time (skeptic runs AFTER review), so for the live loop a downgrade here would generally have no skeptic evidence yet; safe default is to leave this site computing the same reasons unless RE-2 also threads store/slice here. To honor visibility+consistency, RE-2 should route BOTH 4691 and 4970 through the same slice/store-aware wrapper (e.g. reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result, {store, slice}) with the pure 1-arg path preserved).
3) latestRepairReviewContext at src/cli.ts:5104-5112 — repair-prompt context only (status==="accepted" && reasons.length===0 -> undefined). Cosmetic; can keep pure path.

applyReviewOutcome accept path (4724-4735): effectiveStatus==="accepted" -> clearResolvedReviewEscalations + (if not accepted) updateSliceStatus("ready_for_review"); else (4738+) updateSliceStatus(repairing|blocked), updateDependenciesFor blocked, escalation, review.blocked_acceptance event.
result.findingChallengeShape:
RE-1 records skeptic verdicts as EvidenceRecord kind:"finding_challenge" at src/cli.ts:3218-3232 via store.insertEvidence({id, sliceId:slice.id, kind:"finding_challenge", summary:`Skeptic ${status}: ${summary}`, ref:resultPath, payload:{ path, skepticResult, challengedReviewEvidenceId, skepticEvents }, createdAt}). READ THE LATEST EXACTLY like readLatestReviewGate reads review_result: store.listEvidence(slice.id).filter(item => item.kind === "finding_challenge").at(-1), then skepticResultSchema.safeParse(evidence.payload.skepticResult).

skepticResult shape (src/schemas.ts:123-129): { status: upheld|partially_refuted|refuted|uncertain; summary; challengedReviewStatus: accepted|repair_required|blocked|human_required; findingVerdicts: SkepticFindingVerdict[]; recommendation }. EACH verdict (schemas.ts:114-121): { ref?: string (FR/AC ref e.g. "AC-INV-001.1" — present when source==="fr_ac_finding"); dimension?: string (sleuth dimension e.g. "runtime_path" — present when source==="quality_dimension"); source: fr_ac_finding|quality_dimension|required_fix|escalation; verdict: real|refuted|uncertain; severity: blocker|major|minor|nit; reasoning }.

MATCHING for RE-2: a qualityGate-derived blocking reason maps to a verdict where source==="quality_dimension" AND verdict.dimension === dimension.dimension. A blockingConcerns string has no structured ref/dimension, so it can only be matched by source==="quality_dimension" if the skeptic targeted it (otherwise default-keep-blocking). DOWNGRADE only when verdict.verdict==="refuted" (or, per scope, an explicit residual severity minor|nit). KEEP BLOCKING for verdict real|uncertain OR no matching verdict (default-keep-blocking). CRITICAL: skeptic verdicts whose source is fr_ac_finding / required_fix / escalation must NEVER affect the gate's hard backstops — RE-2 consults verdicts ONLY for qualityGate dimensions/blockingConcerns. The fixture skeptic (runFixtureSkeptic, src/cli.ts:4472-4511) emits ALL verdicts as verdict:"uncertain" severity:"minor" — so the fixture path never downgrades (safe). Tests needing a "refuted" verdict must seed a custom skepticResult (write finding_challenge evidence directly) rather than relying on the fixture skeptic.
result.backstops:
HARD BACKSTOPS that must stay unconditional regardless of any skeptic verdict, with cites:
1) SOURCE MUTATION — src/cli.ts:4937 in readLatestReviewGate: `parsed.data.sourceMutationDetected || sourceMutationsAfter.some(item=>item.mutated)` -> status:"human_required". Also reviewResult.sourceMutationDetected field (schemas.ts:93) and the review-time check in applyReviewOutcome:4690. Original mutation detection site is reported at src/cli.ts:4268 (sourceMutationDetected). NEVER downgradeable.
2) HUMAN_REQUIRED / human_input_required — status==="human_required" path in readLatestReviewGate:4945-4951 (status!=="accepted"); per-ref frAcResults statuses human_input_required (verify command at 1111/1146) and awaiting_human_verification. These flow from frAcFindings / human_verification, not qualityGate -> NEVER downgradeable.
3) FAILED / MISSING-EVIDENCE FR/AC COVERAGE — readLatestReviewGate:4953-4961 nonPassingRefs (any slice.frAcRef whose reviewFindingForRef status !== "passed", i.e. failed|missing_evidence|uncertain per schemas.ts:87). reviewFindingForRef at src/cli.ts:5144-5148. frAcFindings status enum is the immutable coverage signal -> NEVER downgradeable.
4) MISSING / UNPARSEABLE STRUCTURED RESULT — readLatestReviewGate schema-fail branch 4926-4933 (blocked) and readAndValidateWorkerResult missing worker_result (src/cli.ts:5221-5237). status!=="accepted" branch (4945) also a structural block. NEVER downgradeable.
5) stubOrHardcodeRisk==="high" (readLatestReviewGate:4962) — NOT in scope to downgrade per current reading (it is not a qualityGate dimension/blockingConcern); keep it unconditional unless RE-2 explicitly classifies it (recommend KEEP blocking).
6) Active acceptance blockers / non-quality escalations in the verify accept formula (src/cli.ts:1058-1060, 1085) — independent of qualityGate; unaffected.
RULE: RE-2 mutates ONLY the qualityGate-derived reasons computed by reviewQualityBlockingReasons (5150). Because the backstops 1-4 are evaluated as SEPARATE early-return branches in readLatestReviewGate BEFORE the qualityGate step (4970), they are structurally immune — the wrapper only needs to filter the qualityGate reasons list and must NOT be inserted before those branches. BACKWARD-COMPAT: when store.listEvidence(slice.id).filter(kind==="finding_challenge") is empty, the wrapper must return the pure reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result) output byte-identically (test c asserts this).
result.recordingHooks:
RECORDING a downgrade has two homes, both pre-existing:
1) residualRisks — reviewResult.qualityGate.residualRisks: string[] (src/schemas.ts:78, in reviewQualityGateSchema; default [] at 95-101). This is the in-result, ledger-visible home the prompt names. To persist a downgrade onto the slice's recorded review, RE-2 appends a human-readable line (e.g. `DOWNGRADED <dimension|ref> by skeptic <actor>: <reasoning>`) to qualityGate.residualRisks. NOTE: the review_result evidence is already written by the time the gate consults the skeptic; to surface a residualRisk the gate/verify path must either (a) write a new evidence/event capturing the downgrade, or (b) RE-2 augments the verify command evidence payload (src/cli.ts:1092-1117, the kind:"command" reviewGate payload) with the recorded downgrades. The cleanest visibility path is the harness event (below) plus appending to a downgrades list inside the reviewGate object that readLatestReviewGate already returns into that command evidence at 1104/1139.
2) HARNESS EVENT — createEvent({actor, type, entityType, entityId, payload}) at src/events.ts:4-20 (auto-fills id+timestamp) + store.addEvent(event) at src/storage.ts:231. RE-2 emits one event per downgrade, e.g. type:"review.finding_downgraded", entityType:"slice", entityId:slice.id, payload:{ dimension?|ref?, fromSeverity, skepticVerdict:"refuted", reasoning, skepticActor, challengeEvidenceId }. Pattern mirrors existing review.blocked_acceptance (src/cli.ts:4760-4773) and skeptic.finding_challenged (3277-3296). 
SKEPTIC ACTOR for the event/visibility: the finding_challenge EvidenceRecord has NO actor field (EvidenceRecord type src/types.ts:171-179 lacks actor) and its payload (3225-3230) does NOT store the skeptic actor — only path/skepticResult/challengedReviewEvidenceId/skepticEvents. The skeptic actor is recoverable from the durable agent-run ledger: store.listAgentRuns().filter(run=>run.sliceId===slice.id && run.role==="skeptic").at(-1).actor (AgentRun carries role/actor/sliceId; created at src/cli.ts:3086-3096). It is ALSO in skeptic.started/completed event payloads as skepticActor (3114, plus 3107 event.actor). RE-2 should EITHER add skepticActor to the finding_challenge payload (small additive edit at 3225) OR recover it from the agent-run ledger — the latter avoids touching RE-1's recording and reuses the same ledger the independence guard uses.
tests: INDEPENDENCE for test (d): reuse the agent-run ledger check from the RE-1 guard (src/cli.ts:3023-3031): a finding_challenge only counts if a skeptic AgentRun (role==='skeptic', sliceId===slice.id) exists whose actor is NOT any worker/reviewer actor for the slice. Since EvidenceRecord has no actor and the payload omits skepticActor, the downgrade path MUST recover/verify the skeptic actor via store.listAgentRuns() (or RE-2 must add skepticActor to the payload). A test seeding finding_challenge evidence with a worker/reviewer actor (or no independent skeptic run) must be IGNORED -> still blocks.

Test (c) BACKWARD-COMPAT: assert the new slice/store-aware wrapper returns EXACTLY reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result) (pure path) when store.listEvidence(slice.id).filter(kind==='finding_challenge') is empty. reviewQualityBlockingReasons is module-private (not exported), so prefer an e2e assertion: run/review with the fixture driver, then verify the verify-command evidence reviewGate.reason is byte-identical with vs without RE-2 wiring (the e2e harness in tests/skeptic-runner.e2e.test.js drives dist/cli.js and reads slice.evidence[kind==='command'].payload.reviewGate).

Tests must SEED a custom skepticResult to get a 'refuted' verdict — the fixture skeptic (src/cli.ts:4472-4511) only ever emits verdict:'uncertain'/severity:'minor', which by design never downgrades. Write finding_challenge evidence directly (matching the 3218-3232 shape: payload.skepticResult with a findingVerdicts entry {source:'quality_dimension', dimension:<exact dimension.dimension>, verdict:'refuted', severity:'minor', reasoning}) plus a skeptic AgentRun with an independent actor.

Test (a): seed a review_result whose qualityGate has a dimension status:'failed' or risk:'high' (so reviewQualityBlockingReasons would block) + a finding_challenge refuting THAT dimension by name -> verify gate passes (slice acceptable) AND a downgrade is recorded (residualRisk entry on the reviewGate payload AND a review.finding_downgraded harness event in the observe snapshot recentEvents).

Test (b) BACKSTOPS: seed a finding_challenge with verdicts trying to 'refute' a source-mutation (sourceMutationDetected:true), a human_required status, and a failed/missing-evidence frAcFinding -> readLatestReviewGate STILL blocks (verify fails) because those are evaluated in early-return branches at 4937/4945/4953 BEFORE the qualityGate step; assert the skeptic verdict is ignored for each.
Test (e): a verdict of 'real' or 'uncertain', or a refuted verdict whose dimension/ref does NOT match any qualityGate blocking reason, does NOT downgrade -> still blocks (default-keep-blocking).

Run npx tsc (typecheck script) until clean, then npm test (builds + runs node --test tests/**/*.test.js). New e2e test belongs in tests/ as a .js file mirroring tests/skeptic-runner.e2e.test.js (setupWorkspace + runSwarm against dist/cli.js).

result.consumptionRule:
CONSUMPTION RULE — how a skeptic verdict maps to and downgrades a quality-gate blocking reason.

INPUTS to the decision (read at gate time, never at review time guarantees):
- reasons[] = the EXACT output of the pure reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result) (cli.ts:5150). Each entry has a known provenance because the function builds it deterministically:
  R1. `qualityGate.status=failed` (from gate.status==="failed")
  R2. a trimmed gate.blockingConcerns[] string (verbatim, no structured ref/dimension)
  R3. `${dim.dimension} ${dim.status}/${dim.risk}: ${dim.finding}` for each gate.dimensions[] with status==="failed" || risk==="high"
- The LATEST finding_challenge evidence for the slice, read the SAME way readLatestReviewGate reads review_result:
  store.listEvidence(slice.id).filter(i => i.kind === "finding_challenge").at(-1), then skepticResultSchema.safeParse(evidence.payload.skepticResult). If absent/unparseable -> treat as NO verdicts (pure path).
- INDEPENDENCE filter (defense in depth atop RE-1): the latest finding_challenge counts ONLY if there exists a skeptic AgentRun for this slice whose actor is NOT a worker/reviewer actor for the slice. Compute via store.listAgentRuns(): skepticRuns = runs where sliceId===slice.id && role==="skeptic"; workerReviewerActors = runs where sliceId===slice.id && (role==="worker"||role==="reviewer") -> set of actors. The challenge is admissible iff some skepticRun exists with actor NOT in workerReviewerActors. If no admissible independent skeptic run -> verdicts are IGNORED entirely (pure path). (We recover the skeptic actor from the agent-run ledger rather than from the finding_challenge payload, which has no actor field — see RECORDING.)

MATCHING a reason to a verdict (only quality_dimension-sourced verdicts are ever consulted):
- Build the candidate verdict set = skepticResult.findingVerdicts.filter(v => v.source === "quality_dimension"). Verdicts with source fr_ac_finding | required_fix | escalation are NEVER consulted by RE-2 (they pertain to backstops / non-quality signals).
- For an R3 dimension reason: it matches a candidate verdict v iff v.dimension === dimension.dimension (exact string equality on the dimension name). Carry the dimension name alongside each R3 reason so matching does not re-parse the formatted string.
- For an R2 blockingConcern reason and the R1 status reason: there is NO structured dimension/ref, so they match a verdict ONLY if a quality_dimension verdict explicitly carries v.dimension equal to a sentinel the skeptic used to target them. Since the skeptic schema gives no such sentinel today, R1 and R2 are by default NEVER matched -> default-keep-blocking. (Documented limitation; a blockingConcern can only be downgraded if a future skeptic emits a quality_dimension verdict whose dimension string equals the concern text — we do attempt that exact-string fallback so it is possible but not relied upon.)

DOWNGRADE PREDICATE (default-keep-blocking):
- A matched reason is DOWNGRADED (removed from the blocking list, recorded as residual) iff the matching verdict has verdict.verdict === "refuted". Per scope we ALSO allow downgrade when verdict.verdict !== "real" AND verdict.severity is "minor" or "nit" AND the skeptic explicitly classified it as residual — but to stay conservative and unambiguous the canonical rule is: DOWNGRADE ONLY ON verdict==="refuted". (verdict==="uncertain" with severity minor/nit does NOT downgrade — uncertain is treated as keep-blocking, matching invariant "real/uncertain leaves blocking".)
- KEEP BLOCKING when: verdict.verdict is "real" or "uncertain"; OR no candidate quality_dimension verdict matches the reason; OR the challenge is inadmissible (no independent skeptic). This is the default for everything not explicitly refuted by an independent skeptic.
- If multiple verdicts match one reason, a single "refuted" is NOT enough if any matching verdict is "real" — keep blocking if ANY matching verdict is real; downgrade only if at least one matching verdict is refuted AND none is real. (Conservative: a real verdict always wins over a refuted one.)

OUTPUT: the gate uses the FILTERED reasons (originals minus downgraded) for its length>0 block decision, and returns the list of downgrades (dimension/concern, fromSeverity, skepticVerdict, reasoning, skepticActor, challengeEvidenceId) so the caller can record them.
result.downgradableVsUnconditional:
EXACT DOWNGRADABLE-vs-UNCONDITIONAL SPLIT.

DOWNGRADABLE (and ONLY these — they are the reasons produced by reviewQualityBlockingReasons from result.qualityGate):
- gate.dimensions[] entries blocking via status==="failed" || risk==="high" (R3) — downgradable when an independent skeptic emits source==="quality_dimension", dimension===that dimension name, verdict==="refuted".
- gate.blockingConcerns[] strings (R2) and gate.status==="failed" (R1) — TECHNICALLY in the quality-gate family and thus in-scope to downgrade, but they carry no structured dimension/ref, so they downgrade ONLY via an exact-string match against a quality_dimension verdict's dimension field. In practice they default-keep-blocking. They are NOT backstops; they are simply hard to target.

UNCONDITIONAL BACKSTOPS — the skeptic can NEVER downgrade/clear these; they are evaluated as early-return branches in readLatestReviewGate BEFORE the qualityGate step (4970), so the RE-2 wrapper is inserted at 4970 ONLY and is structurally incapable of touching them:
1. SOURCE MUTATION — cli.ts:4937: parsed.data.sourceMutationDetected || sourceMutationsAfter.some(mutated) -> status:"human_required". Also applyReviewOutcome:4690. NEVER downgradeable.
2. NON-ACCEPTED REVIEW STATUS — cli.ts:4945: parsed.data.status !== "accepted" (covers blocked/repair_required/human_required). NEVER downgradeable.
3. FAILED / MISSING-EVIDENCE FR/AC COVERAGE — cli.ts:4953: nonPassingRefs = slice.frAcRefs where reviewFindingForRef(frAcFindings,ref)?.status !== "passed" (failed|missing_evidence|uncertain per schemas.ts:87). NEVER downgradeable — even if a skeptic emits a source==="fr_ac_finding" verdict refuting an FR/AC, RE-2 NEVER consults fr_ac_finding verdicts, so coverage stays blocking.
4. MISSING / UNPARSEABLE STRUCTURED RESULT — cli.ts:4926 schema-fail branch; readAndValidateWorkerResult missing worker_result. NEVER downgradeable.
5. stubOrHardcodeRisk==="high" — cli.ts:4962. NOT a qualityGate dimension/concern; KEEP unconditional (RE-2 does not classify it as downgradable).
6. human_input_required / awaiting_human_verification per-ref statuses and active acceptance blockers / non-quality escalations in the verify accept formula (cli.ts:1058-1060,1085). Independent of qualityGate; unaffected.

ENFORCEMENT RULE: RE-2 consults skeptic verdicts ONLY where source==="quality_dimension". Verdicts with source fr_ac_finding|required_fix|escalation are filtered OUT before matching, so a skeptic literally cannot influence backstops 1-6 even if it tries (test (b) proves this). The wrapper only ever filters the reasons array returned by reviewQualityBlockingReasons; it never sees or returns the backstop branches.
result.backwardCompat:
BACKWARD-COMPATIBILITY GUARANTEE (byte-identical no-skeptic path).

The wrapper reviewQualityBlockingDecision(result, ctx?) is constructed so that whenever there is no admissible independent finding_challenge, it returns reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result) UNCHANGED:
- ctx undefined -> immediate return { reasons: reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result), downgrades: [] }.
- ctx present but store.listEvidence(slice.id).filter(kind==="finding_challenge") is empty -> return base reasons untouched.
- finding_challenge present but skepticResultSchema.safeParse fails -> return base reasons untouched (parse failure never downgrades).
- finding_challenge present but inadmissible (no independent skeptic AgentRun, e.g. the only skeptic run's actor equals a worker/reviewer actor) -> return base reasons untouched.
- finding_challenge admissible but no quality_dimension verdict is "refuted" / matches a reason -> base reasons untouched.

Because the returned reasons are produced by FILTERING the exact baseReasons array (same construction, same order, same strings), and filtering removes nothing on the no-skeptic path, the array is identical element-for-element. The three call sites preserve behavior: readLatestReviewGate's 4971 block and applyReviewOutcome's effectiveStatus computation see the same reasons array as today; the only additive change is an optional downgrades field on readLatestReviewGate's return (ignored by all existing consumers). latestRepairReviewContext is left on the pure function.

Invariant restated: behavior changes ONLY when an independent skeptic has actually emitted a quality_dimension verdict with verdict==="refuted" matching a current quality-gate blocking reason. Everything else is a no-op. Test (c) asserts this e2e by comparing the verify-command evidence reviewGate.reason with vs without RE-2 wiring (must be byte-identical), and unit-asserting reviewQualityBlockingDecision(result) === reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result) for fixture ReviewResults across the no-skeptic branches.
result.recording:
RECORDING each downgrade — two visible homes, both pre-existing patterns.

1) residualRisk (in-result, ledger-visible). reviewResult.qualityGate.residualRisks: string[] (schemas.ts:78). The original review_result evidence is already written by review time, so RE-2 does NOT mutate it in place. Instead, the downgrade is surfaced where the gate is consumed:
   - readLatestReviewGate returns the new downgrades[] field. In the verify command (cli.ts:1092-1117) we add the recorded downgrades to the persisted command evidence payload — specifically attach `reviewGate.downgrades` (the GateDowngrade[] already on the returned reviewGate object) and additionally push a human-readable line per downgrade onto a `reviewGateResidualRisks` array in that same command evidence payload, e.g. `DOWNGRADED dimension <name> by skeptic <actor>: <reasoning> (challenge <evidenceId>)`. This is the cleanest visibility path because the command evidence is the gate's authoritative output and is already surfaced in observe snapshots (slice.evidence[kind==="command"].payload.reviewGate). No new schema field is required on reviewResult; we reuse the freeform command-evidence payload + the existing residualRisks vocabulary.

2) HARNESS EVENT (status from the ledger, not chat). Emit one event per downgrade at the verify site (where the gate decision is actually applied), mirroring review.blocked_acceptance (cli.ts:4760) and skeptic.finding_challenged (3277):
   createEvent({ actor: options.actor, type: "review.finding_downgraded", entityType: "slice", entityId: slice.id, payload: { dimension?, concern?, fromSeverity, skepticVerdict: "refuted", reasoning, skepticActor, challengeEvidenceId, reviewEvidenceId } }) then store.addEvent(...). These appear in observe recentEvents so a human sees exactly what the skeptic downgraded and why. Nothing hidden.

SKEPTIC ACTOR for the event/residual line: the finding_challenge EvidenceRecord has NO actor field and its payload (cli.ts:3225-3230) does not store skepticActor. Recover it from the durable agent-run ledger — the SAME ledger the independence guard uses: store.listAgentRuns().filter(run => run.sliceId===slice.id && run.role==="skeptic").at(-1)?.actor. This avoids touching RE-1's recording. (Optional tiny additive improvement: add skepticActor to the finding_challenge payload at 3225 so it is co-located; not required, and recovering from the ledger is preferred to keep RE-1 untouched.)

WHERE recording happens: ONLY in readLatestReviewGate's consumer (the verify command). applyReviewOutcome does NOT record downgrades (no skeptic evidence exists at review time). This keeps recording at the single point where a downgrade actually changes an accept decision.
result.testPlan:
FIXTURE TEST PLAN — deterministic, no provider spend. Two layers.

SEEDING NOTE (critical): the fixture skeptic (runFixtureSkeptic, cli.ts:4472-4511) emits ONLY verdict:"uncertain"/severity:"minor", which by design never downgrades. To get a "refuted" quality_dimension verdict deterministically, add ONE minimal test-support seam: have runFixtureSkeptic honor an env override SWARM_FIXTURE_SKEPTIC_RESULT pointing to a JSON file; when set, the fixture path writes that file's content (validated by skepticResultSchema) as the skepticResult instead of the canned uncertain one. This routes a seeded "refuted" verdict through the REAL independence guard + REAL finding_challenge recording, with no real provider. (Alternative if an env seam is unwanted: a unit-style test that imports dist store API to insertEvidence(finding_challenge) + insertAgentRun(role:"skeptic", independent actor) directly, then calls the verify command. The env seam is preferred — it exercises the real recording path end-to-end.)

NEW e2e file tests/skeptic-gate-consumption.e2e.test.js mirroring tests/skeptic-runner.e2e.test.js (reuse setupWorkspace + runSwarm against dist/cli.js; build first via npm run build).

(a) DOWNGRADE — independent skeptic refutes a quality dimension -> reason no longer blocks -> slice accepts; downgrade recorded.
  - Seed a review_result whose qualityGate has a dimension {dimension:"runtime_path", status:"failed", risk:"high", finding:...} so reviewQualityBlockingReasons would block. (Easiest: run+review with fixture, then craft the skepticResult to refute exactly the dimension the fixture review marks; OR seed a custom review_result. Use the dimension name the fixture reviewer actually emits — grep runFixtureReview to get exact dimension names, then refute that one.)
  - Run skeptic with an INDEPENDENT actor and SWARM_FIXTURE_SKEPTIC_RESULT = a JSON file with findingVerdicts:[{source:"quality_dimension", dimension:"<that name>", verdict:"refuted", severity:"minor", reasoning:"..."}].
  - swarm verify -> assert "Verification passed" and slice.status==="accepted".
  - Assert observe recentEvents includes type:"review.finding_downgraded" with payload.dimension==="<name>", skepticVerdict:"refuted", skepticActor=the independent actor.
  - Assert the latest command evidence payload.reviewGate.downgrades (or reviewGateResidualRisks) contains the downgrade line.

(b) BACKSTOPS — skeptic "refutes" backstops -> STILL BLOCKS.
  - Three sub-cases, seed a finding_challenge (independent actor) whose findingVerdicts try to refute: (i) a source-mutation (seed review_result.sourceMutationDetected:true) using source:"quality_dimension" or even fr_ac_finding; (ii) a non-accepted status / human_required; (iii) a failed/missing_evidence frAcFinding via source:"fr_ac_finding" verdict:"refuted".
  - swarm verify -> assert verification FAILS for each; reviewGate.reason cites the backstop ("immutable source mutation" / non-accepted status / "non-passing FR/AC findings"), NOT a downgrade. Assert NO review.finding_downgraded event for the backstop. Proves backstops are evaluated before 4970 and fr_ac_finding/escalation verdicts are never consulted.

(c) BACKWARD-COMPAT — no finding_challenge -> identical blocking.
  - e2e: run+review+verify a slice with a failing qualityGate dimension and NO skeptic; capture command evidence reviewGate.reason. Then a second identical workspace with the RE-2 build but still no skeptic -> assert reviewGate.reason byte-identical. Also assert the accepted-review case from the existing skeptic-runner (d) test still yields reviewGate.reason==="latest review accepted" (regression). Plus a unit assertion (import dist) that reviewQualityBlockingDecision(result) deep-equals reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result) when ctx omitted and when store has zero finding_challenge.

(d) INDEPENDENCE — non-independent challenge is IGNORED -> still blocks.
  - Seed a finding_challenge with a "refuted" quality_dimension verdict BUT make the only skeptic AgentRun's actor equal a worker/reviewer actor (or have no skeptic run at all — directly insert finding_challenge without a skeptic run). Since the live guard rejects reused actors, simulate by direct store seeding. swarm verify -> assert it STILL BLOCKS (the downgrade is ignored because admissibility fails) and NO review.finding_downgraded event.

(e) REAL/UNCERTAIN OR UNMATCHED -> no downgrade, still blocks.
  - Independent skeptic, but verdict:"real" (sub-case 1) and verdict:"uncertain" (sub-case 2) on the matching dimension; plus sub-case 3: verdict:"refuted" but dimension does NOT match any blocking reason (e.g. dimension:"some_other"). For all three: swarm verify -> STILL BLOCKS, reviewGate.reason cites the original quality reason, NO review.finding_downgraded event.

RUN: npx tsc (typecheck) until clean, then npm test (builds dist + node --test tests/**/*.test.js). Confirm the existing tests/skeptic-runner.e2e.test.js (esp. its (d) additivity test) still passes unchanged.
risks: MATCHING FRAGILITY: R3 reasons are matched by dimension NAME equality. If two qualityGate dimensions share a name, a single refuted verdict would downgrade both. Mitigate by matching on the dimension object identity/index where possible, or document that dimension names must be unique (they are emitted per-dimension by the reviewer).

BLOCKINGCONCERNS/STATUS (R1,R2) are effectively non-downgradable because they carry no structured dimension — acceptable per scope (default-keep-blocking) but means a skeptic cannot clear a free-text blockingConcern even if genuinely refuted. Documented as a limitation; a future schema change could let the skeptic target concerns by an explicit ref.

SKEPTIC ACTOR RECOVERY relies on the agent-run ledger (listAgentRuns) since finding_challenge has no actor. If the finding_challenge was seeded without a corresponding independent skeptic AgentRun, recovery yields undefined and the challenge is correctly treated as inadmissible (keeps blocking) — but tests must seed the AgentRun too, or rely on the env-override path that creates a real run.

applyReviewOutcome runs at REVIEW time (before the skeptic), so threading it through the wrapper is a no-op today; if a future change runs the skeptic before review, applyReviewOutcome would start downgrading without recording. Mitigate by keeping recording at the verify consumer and adding a note that applyReviewOutcome intentionally does not record.

ORDERING/LATEST semantics: only the LATEST finding_challenge is consulted (mirrors latest review_result). If a slice is re-reviewed after a skeptic challenge, a stale challenge could match a new review's dimension by name and wrongly downgrade. Mitigate by tying the challenge to challengedReviewEvidenceId === the latest review_result evidence id; only consult a finding_challenge whose payload.challengedReviewEvidenceId equals the review_result evidence the gate is reading. This closes a real safety hole and should be part of admissibility.

TEST SEAM (SWARM_FIXTURE_SKEPTIC_RESULT env or direct store seeding) must not leak into production behavior — gate it strictly to driver==="fixture" and only when the env var is set, so non-test fixture runs keep emitting the canned uncertain result.

Adding downgrades[] to readLatestReviewGate's return type touches a widely-read shape; keep it OPTIONAL and ensure no existing consumer destructures exhaustively. The verify command and any web/observe serializers should tolerate the new field (it is plain JSON in command evidence payload).

result.summary:
Implemented RE-2: the quality gate now consults the LATEST independent finding_challenge (skeptic) evidence to downgrade ONLY quality-gate findings the skeptic explicitly refuted, while hard backstops stay unconditional, the no-skeptic path is byte-identical, and every downgrade is recorded.

Added a slice/store-aware wrapper reviewQualityBlockingDecision(result, ctx?) (src/cli.ts) that returns { reasons, downgrades }. The pure reviewQualityBlockingReasons is left byte-for-byte untouched (still the single source of truth, still used by latestRepairReviewContext). A new reviewQualityBlockingReasonsStructured mirror carries provenance (R1=status, R2=concern, R3=dimension) so matching does not re-parse formatted strings; it constructs identical `reason` strings in identical order, so filtering yields byte-identical reasons on the no-skeptic path.

Consumption rule (default-keep-blocking): a quality reason is downgraded ONLY when an admissible independent skeptic emitted a source==='quality_dimension' verdict with verdict==='refuted' (dimension-name exact match; concern/status only via exact-string fallback) AND no matching 'real' verdict exists. 'real'/'uncertain'/unmatched leave it blocking.

Admissibility (four gates, any miss => pure path): latest finding_challenge exists+parses; payload.challengedReviewEvidenceId equals the review_result being gated (closes the stale-challenge ordering hole, risks#5); an INDEPENDENT skeptic AgentRun exists in the ledger (actor not in the slice's worker/reviewer actor set) — the skeptic actor is recovered from the agent-run ledger since finding_challenge has no actor field; only quality_dimension verdicts are consulted (fr_ac_finding/required_fix/escalation are filtered out before matching).

Wiring: readLatestReviewGate now calls the wrapper at the qualityGate step ONLY (after all backstop early-returns), and its return type gains an optional downgrades?: GateDowngrade[] (purely additive). applyReviewOutcome routes through the wrapper for single-source-of-truth but does NOT record (no skeptic evidence exists at review time). All four backstop branches (source mutation, non-accepted status, non-passing FR/AC coverage, schema-fail) plus stubOrHardcodeRisk remain before the wrapper and are structurally immune.

Recording (visibility, two homes) happens ONLY at the verify consumer: one harness event review.finding_downgraded per downgrade (payload: dimension/concern, targetKind, fromSeverity, skepticVerdict, reasoning, skepticActor, challengeEvidenceId, reviewEvidenceId) and a reviewGateResidualRisks string[] of human-readable DOWNGRADED lines added to both the command evidence payload and the verification.completed event payload; reviewGate.downgrades also rides along in the command evidence.

Added a strictly fixture-only, env-gated test seam loadSeededFixtureSkepticResult() (reads SWARM_FIXTURE_SKEPTIC_RESULT, validates via skepticResultSchema) so a seeded 'refuted' verdict routes through the REAL independence guard + REAL finding_challenge recording with no provider spend; absent the env var, the canned fixture (uncertain) result is unchanged.
result.downgradeRule: A quality-gate blocking reason is downgraded (removed from the blocking list, recorded as a residual) iff: (1) ctx is provided with store+slice; (2) the latest finding_challenge evidence for the slice exists and its payload.skepticResult parses against skepticResultSchema; (3) when a reviewEvidenceId is supplied, the challenge's payload.challengedReviewEvidenceId equals it (stale challenges ignored); (4) an independent skeptic AgentRun exists for the slice whose actor is NOT a worker/reviewer actor for the slice; (5) a verdict with source==='quality_dimension' matches the reason by exact dimension-name equality (concern/status only via exact-string fallback), with verdict.verdict==='refuted' and NO matching verdict with verdict==='real'. A 'real' verdict always wins over a 'refuted' one; 'uncertain' and unmatched verdicts never downgrade. Any admissibility miss returns reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result) unchanged.
result.recordingAdded: Each downgrade is recorded at the verify consumer in two ledger-visible homes: (1) a harness event type 'review.finding_downgraded' (entityType slice, payload { dimension|concern, targetKind, fromSeverity, skepticVerdict:'refuted', reasoning, skepticActor, challengeEvidenceId, reviewEvidenceId }) emitted via store.addEvent so it appears in observe recentEvents; (2) a reviewGateResidualRisks string[] of 'DOWNGRADED <kind> <target> (<fromSeverity>) by skeptic <actor>: <reasoning> (challenge <evidenceId>)' lines attached to both the command (verification) evidence payload and the verification.completed event payload, plus reviewGate.downgrades (the GateDowngrade[]) carried in the command evidence. applyReviewOutcome intentionally does NOT record (no skeptic evidence exists at review time).

result.evidence:
The sole authoritative acceptance decision is the verify command at src/cli.ts:1114: `const passed = commandPassed && workerGate.passed && reviewGate.passed && activeAcceptanceBlockers.length === 0 && perRefPassed;`. It is the ONLY path that sets a slice to "accepted" (src/cli.ts:1116; a grep of all updateSliceStatus(...,"accepted") call sites confirms no other acceptance path — applyReviewOutcome only ever reaches "ready_for_review" at :4787, the skeptic command never calls updateSliceStatus, and recovery at :1637 only sets closed/blocked). The skeptic can influence ONLY the `reviewGate.passed` term. The other four AND-terms are skeptic-free:

1. SOURCE MUTATION backstop — readLatestReviewGate (src/cli.ts:4998-5005) returns {passed:false,status:"human_required"} when sourceMutationDetected, and this RETURNS before any skeptic consultation (the only skeptic call, reviewQualityBlockingDecision, is at :5033, strictly after). The review-time consumer applyReviewOutcome computes sourceMutationDetected independently (:4744) and forces effectiveStatus="human_required" FIRST in the ternary (:4753), so a downgraded quality reason cannot override it.

2. NON-ACCEPTED STATUS / human_required backstop — readLatestReviewGate :5006-5013 returns the raw review status (blocked/repair_required/human_required) and RETURNS before :5033.

3. FAILED / MISSING-EVIDENCE FR/AC backstop — two independent mechanisms: (a) readLatestReviewGate :5014-5022 returns blocked for any non-passing frAcFinding, before the skeptic call; (b) perRefPassed (:1113) requires every ref status to be "passed"/"overridden", derived from buildFrAcResults (:5532) which sources status purely from workerGate.frAcResults + commandPassed; readAndValidateWorkerResult (:5418-5517) reads only worker_result evidence and never touches finding_challenge. The only reviewGate read in buildFrAcResults (:5567) can at most mark a ref awaiting_human_verification (which makes perRefPassed FALSE — strictly harder to accept), never upgrade a failed/missing ref to passed.

4. MISSING STRUCTURED EVIDENCE backstop — schema-fail / missing worker_result / missing review_result all return passed:false in readLatestReviewGate (:4987) and readAndValidateWorkerResult (:5427-5462) before any skeptic logic.

The skeptic consumer reviewQualityBlockingDecision (:5285-5359) is structurally confined: it operates only on reviewQualityBlockingReasonsStructured (:5257), built solely from result.qualityGate (status/blockingConcerns/dimensions, :5219-5231 base; mirror :5257), and at :5330 filters findingVerdicts to source==="quality_dimension" ONLY — so fr_ac_finding/required_fix/escalation verdicts are never consulted (schema enum at src/schemas.ts:117 makes source a discriminator). Conservative semantics: a "real" verdict beats "refuted" and "uncertain" never downgrades (:5341-5342). It also requires an independent skeptic AgentRun whose actor is not a worker/reviewer actor (:5317-5324) and that the challenge targeted the same reviewEvidenceId (:5306-5311, defeating stale-challenge collisions).

The skeptic command itself is read-only w.r.t. gate state: src/cli.ts:3250-3268 inserts only finding_challenge evidence + events/heartbeats and DELIBERATELY does NOT call applyReviewOutcome/updateSliceStatus/updateDependenciesFor/insertReviewEscalation (:3252-3253) — so it cannot clear the activeAcceptanceBlockers (:1087-1089, which count blocker/human_required/critical escalations). The only escalation-clearing reachable elsewhere either excludes human_required/critical (clearResolvedReviewEscalations :4840 clears only warning/blocker, called from applyReviewOutcome) or is gated to recovery restart/revive matching a stale/recovery needle on a superseded run id (clearSupersededRecoveryEscalations :2030-2034) — neither is skeptic-reachable nor can clear a source-mutation/FR-AC/review human_required blocker.

Corroborated by tests/skeptic-gate-consumption.e2e.test.js:135-195 which exercises (b.i) source-mutation and (b.ii) refuted fr_ac_finding and asserts the slice stays non-accepted with no downgrade event.
result.gaps: No invariant-breaking case found. Minor notes (not violations): (1) The review-time consumer applyReviewOutcome (src/cli.ts:4749) calls reviewQualityBlockingDecision WITHOUT passing reviewEvidenceId, so the stale-challenge same-review guard (:5306-5311) is skipped there; in principle a stale finding_challenge could downgrade a quality reason at review time. This is benign for the invariant because (a) review time never produces "accepted" (max is ready_for_review, :4787), (b) source mutation is checked first and independently in the ternary (:4753), and (c) the authoritative verify gate re-evaluates with the guard. (2) A quality_dimension verdict with dimension set to the literal status string "failed" (or a concern's text) can downgrade the qualityGate.status/blockingConcern reason via the exact-string match at :5338; this is explicitly within the permitted quality-gate scope (qualityGate dimensions + blockingConcerns + status are sleuth quality findings), not a hard backstop, so it does not weaken the invariant. (3) I did not execute the test suite; findings are from static control-flow tracing plus the asserting e2e test text.

result.invariant: DEFAULT-KEEP-BLOCKING: at the acceptance boundary, only an EXPLICIT skeptic "refuted" verdict that MATCHES a quality-gate blocking reason from an admissible independent challenge may downgrade it; real/uncertain/unmatched verdicts (and the no-skeptic path) keep blocking, and every downgrade is recorded (no silent weakening).
result.evidence:
The only state transition to "accepted" is src/cli.ts:1116 inside `verify`, which sets accepted only when `passed` (line 1114) AND `reviewGate.passed`. `reviewGate` comes from `readLatestReviewGate` (line 1057), which: evaluates ALL hard backstops BEFORE consulting any challenge — schema failure (4987), source mutation -> human_required (4998-5005), review status != accepted (5006-5013), non-passing FR/AC refs (5014-5022), high stub/hardcode (5023-5030) — and ONLY THEN calls `reviewQualityBlockingDecision` (5033) passing `reviewEvidenceId` (5036).

`reviewQualityBlockingDecision` (5285-5360) is default-keep-blocking by construction: it starts from `baseReasons = reviewQualityBlockingReasons(result)` (5289) and returns them UNCHANGED on every early exit — no ctx (5290), no finding_challenge (5298), unparseable skeptic result (5301), stale challenge whose `challengedReviewEvidenceId != reviewEvidenceId` (5306-5311), or no independent skeptic run (5324). A reason is dropped ONLY when a `source=="quality_dimension"` verdict (filter at 5330 excludes fr_ac_finding/required_fix/escalation, protecting hard backstops) EXACTLY matches the reason's target (5338) AND has verdict "refuted" AND no "real" verdict for the same target (5339-5342: `if (refuting && !anyReal)`). Everything else is pushed to `keptReasons` (5353), so uncertain/real/unmatched still block.

Tests corroborate the CLI-reachable behavior: (b) source-mutation/failed-FR-AC backstops cannot be downgraded; (c) no-challenge path is byte-identical; (d) a non-independent challenge is ignored; (e) real/uncertain/unmatched all keep blocking with zero downgrade events (tests/skeptic-gate-consumption.e2e.test.js:135-323). Visibility holds: each downgrade emits a `review.finding_downgraded` event and a `DOWNGRADED ...` residualRisk line at the single accept consumer (src/cli.ts:1061-1086,1134). `finding_challenge` evidence is written in exactly ONE place (src/cli.ts:3258) guarded by the live independence check (src/cli.ts:3054-3062) that rejects any worker/reviewer actor before any write, so via the CLI every challenge author is a verified-independent skeptic. I could not construct a CLI-reachable case where a real/uncertain/unmatched finding, or a no/stale-skeptic state, yields an accepted slice.
result.gaps:
Three real DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH defects that do NOT break the acceptance boundary via the CLI but weaken the surrounding guarantees; worth fixing:

1) Review-time staleness gap (src/cli.ts:4749). `applyReviewOutcome` calls `reviewQualityBlockingDecision` WITHOUT `reviewEvidenceId`, so the staleness guard (5306-5311) is skipped. On a RE-REVIEW, a finding_challenge from a PRIOR review cycle (latest by `.at(-1)`, 5294-5297) can match the new review's quality reasons by dimension-name collision and flip the review-time `effectiveStatus` to "accepted", moving the slice to `ready_for_review` (4787) and clearing blocker escalations (4786) while SUPPRESSING the new blocker escalation (4764 skipped). This is a silent weakening of intermediate state. It does not produce an accepted slice because `verify` (the only accept transition, 1116) re-gates with `reviewEvidenceId` passed (5036) and re-blocks the stale challenge — but the comment at 4745-4748 asserts "no finding_challenge exists" which is FALSE on re-reviews. Fix: pass `reviewEvidenceId: input.reviewEvidenceId` at 4749.

2) Independence decoupled from challenge authorship (src/cli.ts:5314-5325). The gate verifies that SOME independent skeptic run EXISTS for the slice (5321-5324), but never that the SELECTED challenge (`.at(-1)` finding_challenge, 5294-5297) was authored by that independent run (finding_challenge carries no actor, per comment 5315-5316). If a non-independent challenge is in the ledger AND any unrelated independent skeptic run coexists, the non-independent challenge's "refuted" verdicts are honored and the downgrade is MISATTRIBUTED to the independent actor (`skepticActor = independentSkepticRun.actor`, 5325), producing false provenance in the recorded residualRisk/event. Test (d) only covers the case where the lone skeptic run is non-independent. Reaching this needs a non-independent challenge in the ledger, which the live CLI guard (3058) prevents at write time, so it is direct-seed-only today — but the defense-in-depth check is incomplete.

3) Status-scope breadth (src/cli.ts:5260-5261, 5338, 5342). The downgradable set includes a synthetic "status" entry (target == `gate.status`, i.e. the literal "failed"), so a `quality_dimension` verdict with `dimension:"failed"` can clear `qualityGate.status=failed` even when there are no failing dimensions/concerns — i.e. the skeptic nulls the gate's holistic verdict by string-matching "failed" rather than independently assessing a concrete dimension. The non-negotiable enumerates the downgradable set as "qualityGate dimensions + blockingConcerns" and does not list qualityGate.status. It still requires an explicit refuted verdict and is recorded, so it does not break DEFAULT-KEEP-BLOCKING, but it is broader than the stated scope and lets a literal-"failed" match clear a holistic block.

result.invariant: INDEPENDENCE: only a finding_challenge from an independent skeptic actor (never the slice worker/reviewer actor) can downgrade a quality-gate finding.
result.evidence:
The implementation does NOT guarantee that the downgrade-driving challenge came from an independent actor. The independence credential and the downgrade verdicts are DECOUPLED, and the RE-1 guard is one-directional, so a non-independent actor can drive a downgrade. I demonstrated this end-to-end (slice ACCEPTED, dimension downgraded by a worker actor's verdict).

ROOT CAUSE (x:/repositories/agent-swarm/src/cli.ts, reviewQualityBlockingDecision):
- Lines 5294-5297: the downgrade VERDICTS are taken from the LATEST finding_challenge evidence for the slice, regardless of who authored it.
- Line 5316 comment + storage: finding_challenge evidence has NO actor/runId field. It inserts only path/skepticResult/challengedReviewEvidenceId/skepticEvents (src/cli.ts:3255-3268). So the challenge author cannot be identified from the evidence.
- Lines 5317-5325: INDEPENDENCE is established by finding ANY skeptic-role AgentRun for the slice whose actor is not a worker/reviewer (independentSkepticRun.at(-1)). It is never checked that this run is the AUTHOR of the latest finding_challenge.
- Line 5325 vs 5330/5340-5350: skepticActor (the recorded "who downgraded") comes from the unrelated independentSkepticRun, while the verdicts/challengeEvidenceId driving the downgrade come from the latest challengeEvidence. The two are matched ONLY by "same slice."

ONE-DIRECTIONAL GUARD (enables the actor to be both skeptic and worker):
- The only independence guard is in executeSkepticRun (src/cli.ts:3054-3062): it rejects a skeptic --actor that is ALREADY a worker/reviewer. It does NOT prevent the reverse.
- executeWorkerRun (src/cli.ts:2447-2509) and executeReviewRun (src/cli.ts:2704-2760) have NO guard against an actor who previously ran as a skeptic. So an actor can run skeptic FIRST (passing the guard) and become a worker/reviewer AFTER.

CONSUMER does not re-check (src/cli.ts:1057-1086): the verify consumer only RECORDS reviewGate.downgrades; it performs no independence re-validation of the challenge author.

DEMONSTRATED (reproduction via production CLI commands only, fixture driver, no DB-forged challenge):
1) honest-worker runs work; honest-reviewer reviews; a review_result with a failing/high runtime_path quality dimension is the latest review.
2) honest-skeptic (independent) runs skeptic, verdict "uncertain" (does NOT refute).
3) actor-mallory runs `swarm skeptic` (allowed: not yet a worker/reviewer) and REFUTES the dimension -> authors the LATEST finding_challenge.
4) actor-mallory then runs `swarm run` as WORKER on the same slice -> NO guard blocks it; mallory is now a worker (non-independent).
5) `swarm verify` -> slice ACCEPTED, reviewGate.passed=true, downgrade applied. Output: downgrades=[{target:"runtime_path", skepticVerdict:"refuted", reasoning:"self-clearing", skepticActor:"honest-skeptic", ...}]. The reasoning "self-clearing" is MALLORY's verdict text, but skepticActor is recorded as the unrelated "honest-skeptic". A non-independent actor (worker + challenge author) caused the acceptance, and the visibility ledger names the wrong (innocent) actor.

This breaks INDEPENDENCE two ways: (a) functionally, a worker/reviewer actor's own challenge verdict downgraded a finding; (b) VISIBILITY, the residualRisk/event attributes the downgrade to an innocent independent actor (honest-skeptic), masking who actually cleared it.
result.gaps:
CONCRETE FIX REQUIRED: bind the independence credential to the AUTHOR of the consumed challenge, not to "any independent skeptic run for the slice."
- Persist the authoring actor (or runId) ON the finding_challenge evidence at insert (src/cli.ts:3255-3268 currently omits it), then in reviewQualityBlockingDecision require that the latest challenge's OWN author is a skeptic-role run AND that author is not in workerReviewerActors. Today the verdicts (latest challenge) and the independence proof (independentSkepticRun) are sourced separately (cli.ts:5294-5297 vs 5321-5325).
- Add the reverse guard: executeWorkerRun (cli.ts:2447) and executeReviewRun (cli.ts:2704) must reject an actor who previously ran as a skeptic on the slice, OR — better — the gate must treat the challenge author's later worker/reviewer role as disqualifying (which it would, automatically, once independence is checked against the author rather than an unrelated run).

SCOPE OF MY CHECK: read-only static review + an executed CLI reproduction with the fixture driver and the SWARM_FIXTURE_SKEPTIC_RESULT seam. I did not test with real codex/claude drivers (behavior is driver-agnostic at the gate, so this is not load-bearing). Existing test (d) (tests/skeptic-gate-consumption.e2e.test.js:229) only covers the case where the ONLY skeptic run reuses the worker actor; it does NOT cover the decoupling case (independent honest skeptic present + non-independent challenge author), which is exactly the hole. The stale-challenge guard (cli.ts:5306-5311) does block a variant where a NEW review is seeded after the malicious challenge, but does NOT block the demonstrated path where the malicious challenge targets the current/latest review and the author becomes a worker afterward.

result.gaps:
No way found to weaken acceptance on the strict no-finding_challenge path; the invariant holds. Adjacent observations (NOT violations of this invariant, but worth noting):
1) Scope nuance: "byte-identical" is true for the BLOCKING DECISION (passed/status/reason and slice status) and for the array of quality reasons. The serialized command-evidence payload is NOT byte-identical to pre-RE-2 — RE-2 adds reviewGate.downgrades (=[]) and reviewGateResidualRisks (=[]). These are additive observability fields and do not change any accept/block outcome, so the decision-level invariant holds; only the persisted payload shape grew.
2) The review-time consumer applyReviewOutcome (cli.ts:4749) calls reviewQualityBlockingDecision WITHOUT reviewEvidenceId, so the stale-challenge ordering guard (5306-5312) is bypassed there. This is safe for THIS invariant (no challenge => early-return at 5298 before the guard matters), but it is a real divergence from the verify consumer's hardening: if a stale finding_challenge from a prior review iteration exists at a later review time, the review-time escalation/effectiveStatus path could consult it without the same-review-id check. That is outside this invariant (it requires a challenge to exist) but is a latent inconsistency the skeptic-review phase for a DIFFERENT invariant (ordering/latest-challenge) should examine.
3) Test (c) proves determinism across two RE-2 runs, not a literal pre-RE-2 baseline diff; I closed that gap myself with the stash-based differential run above.
